product.name: Reconciliation Through Relationships Design System
product.description: A standalone, manifest-driven catalog for RTR foundations, components, validation, and browser tests.

foundations.name: Principles
foundations.description: Three principles govern every design decision in RTR. When a component page and a principle disagree, the principle wins.

foundations.name: Design tokens
foundations.description: All visual decisions flow from one token file. Components consume semantic roles like --primary and --card, never raw palette values.

foundations.name: Color
foundations.description: A palette drawn from the land: spruce forest, birchbark, prairie ochre, river water, wild berry. Every hue carries a fixed meaning, and status is never colour alone.

foundations.name: Typography
foundations.description: Two typefaces divide the work: Fraunces carries the voice and Atkinson Hyperlegible carries the reading, at generous sizes.
highlights: Fraunces for voice, Atkinson for reading.

foundations.name: Layout & spacing
foundations.description: Calm, single-minded layout: one column of content on a birch page, parchment surfaces for anything that groups, and a 4px spacing scale.

foundations.name: Brand & motifs
foundations.description: Three geometric motifs: the open-circle mark, the woven strand, and the panel-on-dark figure. Abstract by design, never appropriated artwork.

foundations.name: Iconography
foundations.description: A single consistent family of 2px-stroke outline icons from Lucide. Icons support text; they never replace it except in labelled icon buttons.
highlights: Pair icons with words where needed.

foundations.name: Accessibility
foundations.description: Accessibility commitments are design constraints: readable type, visible focus, real labels, reduced-motion support, and plain language.

categories.label: Form controls
categories.description: Text entry, selection, and validation patterns.

categories.label: Navigation
categories.description: Headers, tabs, menus, sheets, and wayfinding.

categories.description: Cards, separators, tables, rows, and page framing.

categories.label: Popups & feedback

components.name: Button
components.description: A button is a promise about what happens next, so its label names the action’s **result** — “Schedule call,” “Begin your journey,” never “Submit” or “OK.” Visual weight communicates importance: exactly one solid primary button per view, with every other action stepping down to outline, soft, quiet, or link.

attributes.description: Renders the control as a link

api.name: Usage
api.description: Primary and secondary actions.

components.name: Form field
components.description: A form field is a **composition**, not a single component: a label, a control, optional hint text, and — when validation fails — an error message, wired together for the screen reader.

api.name: Usage
api.description: A field is four parts stacked with an 8px gap: label, control, optional hint, and — when validation fails — an error message wired to the control with aria-describedby.

components.name: Input
components.description: Input is a thin styling layer over the native <input>: it forwards type, value, placeholder, and every other input attribute untouched, and paints on the RTR control look. Pair it with a Label and, when a submit fails, a berry error message — see the form field pattern for the full assembly.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Input is a thin styling layer over the native <input>: it forwards type, value, placeholder, and every other input attribute untouched, and paints on the RTR control look. Pair it with a Label and, when a submit fails, a berry error message — see the form field pattern for the full assembly.

components.name: Textarea
components.description: Textarea shares every visual token with Input — parchment fill, 1.5px border-strong border, 10px radius, spruce hover/focus border, ochre focus outline, berry aria-invalid state — through the shared controlStyles. It adds three things: a taller minimum height, a relaxed line height for reading prose, and a vertical resize handle.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Textarea shares every visual token with Input — parchment fill, 1.5px border-strong border, 10px radius, spruce hover/focus border, ochre focus outline, berry aria-invalid state — through the shared controlStyles. It adds three things: a taller minimum height, a relaxed line height for reading prose, and a vertical resize handle.

components.name: Select
components.description: Select is not one component but a set of parts you compose, the same shape as Base UI's own API. The trigger wears the shared control contract (parchment fill, 1.5px border-strong border, 10px radius, spruce hover/focus border, ochre focus outline), so a closed select is visually a sibling of an Input. Use it when the options are a fixed, known set — provinces, formats — and a free-text Input otherwise.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Select is not one component but a set of parts you compose, the same shape as Base UI's own API. The trigger wears the shared control contract (parchment fill, 1.5px border-strong border, 10px radius, spruce hover/focus border, ochre focus outline), so a closed select is visually a sibling of an Input. Use it when the options are a fixed, known set — provinces, formats — and a free-text Input otherwise.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Use a checkbox for options that are **independent** — any number can be on at once (availability days, preferred formats, participation categories). When the options are mutually exclusive, use a Radio group; when a single setting flips a behavior on or off, use a Switch.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Use a checkbox for options that are **independent** — any number can be on at once (availability days, preferred formats, participation categories). When the options are mutually exclusive, use a Radio group; when a single setting flips a behavior on or off, use a Switch.

components.name: Radio group
components.description: Use a radio group when the options are **mutually exclusive** and few enough to show all at once — "Are you Indigenous? Yes / No", "Sex", "Preferred connection format". For independent options where any number can be on, use Checkbox; for a long list, use Select.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Use a fieldset + legend for grouped single-choice options.

components.name: Switch
components.description: Use a switch for a setting that reads naturally as **on or off** and whose label names a state, not a choice: "Auto-matching enabled", "Show me on the regional map". For picking among options use a Radio group or Checkbox; the switch is for behaviors you turn on and off.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Use a switch for a setting that reads naturally as **on or off** and whose label names a state, not a choice: "Auto-matching enabled", "Show me on the regional map". For picking among options use a Radio group or Checkbox; the switch is for behaviors you turn on and off.

components.name: Slider
components.description: Reach for a slider when a rough position along a range is more meaningful than a typed number and the exact value matters less than the sense of "more or less". When the precise number matters — and cohort threshold is a borderline case — a number Input is often clearer, so always pair a slider with a visible read-out of its current value.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Pair range input with visible value text.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A badge summarizes one fact about the thing it sits on. The two families answer two different questions. **Caption badges** (13.5px, no dot) describe or filter — a person’s background, an interest, an active filter. **Status pills** (12.5px, with a 7px leading dot) report where someone is on their journey.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Avatars are **initials only, by design**. On this platform a photo is something you share inside a conversation once both people have agreed to connect — it is never displayed by the system beforehand. Initials keep every list, card, and table warm and personal without pre-empting that consent.

components.name: Progress
components.description: Progress on this platform is about a person’s path, not a loading state. The bar is a 10px sand track with a spruce-600 fill — calm, warm, and paired with a label row that says the same thing in words (“2 of 4 modules”) so the number is never left to the eye alone.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: A skeleton mirrors the layout it replaces — same box sizes, same rhythm — in the muted sand color, pulsing gently until the real content arrives. It reassures without demanding attention, and it keeps the page from reflowing when content lands.

components.name: App header
components.description: AppHeader is one component that every top-level surface wraps with its own links and actions. It is a spruce-800 bar, sticky to the top of the viewport, finished with a **3px ochre bottom strand** (border-ochre-600) that ties the header to the brand’s two-strand motif. The wordmark sits at the left, the primary nav fills the middle, and role and account controls collect on the right.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Sticky spruce shell header with brand, navigation, and actions.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: A tab set is a horizontal row of triggers over a shared bottom rule. The active trigger draws an **ochre-700 underline** (--secondary-foreground) and darkens its label to heading weight; the rest sit in muted text until hovered. Tabs are for switching between peer views of the same data — the dashboard’s Recommended / Connections / All participants — not for navigating between pages, which belongs to the app header.

api.name: Usage
api.description: A tab set is a horizontal row of triggers over a shared bottom rule. The active trigger draws an **ochre-700 underline** (--secondary-foreground) and darkens its label to heading weight; the rest sit in muted text until hovered. components.name: Sheet
components.description: A Sheet is a Dialog that enters from a screen edge rather than the center. Its one shipped job is **mobile navigation**: below 861px the app header hides its inline nav and a Menu button opens a right-side Sheet holding the same links. The panel is a --popover surface by default; the header recolours it to spruce-800 so the mobile nav matches the bar it came from.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Edge-anchored supporting panel for mobile navigation.

components.name: Dropdown menu
components.description: A dropdown menu is a **parchment popup** (--popover) with 4px of padding, a rounded-lg corner, a hairline ring-foreground/10 ring, and a soft shadow. It collects the actions that would otherwise crowd the header — viewing a profile, signing out — behind a single avatar button. Items highlight on focus; the one destructive action, **Sign out**, is drawn in berry.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Short action list anchored to a trigger.

components.name: Breadcrumb & pagination
components.description: Breadcrumbs and pagination answer *where am I* and *how do I move through this*. Both are secondary to the app header and tabs: reach for them only inside long facilitator tables and drill-down views, where a title alone no longer locates the reader.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Wayfinding for deeper facilitator workflows.

components.name: Navigation menu
components.description: A hover/focus-driven menu bar with animated flyout panels. Retained in the library but not used in the shipped product, whose flat navigation lives in the app header and mobile sheet.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Secondary navigation within a section.

components.name: Card
components.description: Cards are the workhorses of the interface, and their guiding rule is that they **lead with the person**. A participant or match card opens with the avatar and name — the record details (status, region, match score) follow. The surface is parchment with a 1px border, a 16px radius, and shadow-rtr-1; on an interactive card the border warms to spruce as you hover.

api.name: Usage

components.name: Separator
components.description: A separator is the quietest divider in the system: a single hairline in the --border color. Use it to separate sections that already belong together — rows in a settings list, groups of links in a footer. When content needs a heavier boundary, that is a job for a Card or spacing, not a rule.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Low-emphasis divider between related content.

components.name: Table
components.description: Tables are for **facilitator views only**. Participants never see each other in a grid — they meet through cards and list rows. When a facilitator does need to scan many people at once, the table keeps the platform’s warmth: uppercase birch headers sit lightly above the rows, and every row opens with the person — a small avatar and name — before any status or date.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Dense facilitator data view.

components.name: List row
components.description: The list row is the participant-facing counterpart to a table row. Where a table packs people into a grid for a facilitator to scan, a list row gives each person their own soft card-like row — avatar, name, a line of context, and a trailing status. The **entire row is one link**, so there is a single, generous target and nothing to hunt for.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Whole-row target for a single item.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: An empty state is a moment of waiting, not a failure, and the panel is written to feel that way: the muted brand mark — a circle still waiting to form — sits above a calm heading and a sentence that explains *why* it’s empty and what happens next. Because relationships in this product genuinely take time, most empty states reassure rather than prompt; an action is offered only when there’s a useful next step.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Explain what is missing and how to proceed.

components.name: Page intro
components.description: Every page begins the same way, so people always know where the content starts: a small ochre **eyebrow** names the section, a Fraunces **heading** names the page, an optional **lead** sets the tone in one sentence, and a woven strand closes the unit like a threshold crossed. Actions — a primary button, or a small settings control — sit to the right on wide screens and drop below the heading on narrow ones.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Eyebrow, heading, lead, weave, and actions.

components.name: App footer
components.description: The footer is a bg-spruce-900 band that mirrors the app header at the other end of the page. It carries the panel-on-dark figure — the faint facing-profiles motif — behind its content, closes with the on-dark weave, and always ends on the **territorial acknowledgment**. It is pinned to the bottom of short pages with mt-auto.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Mission copy and territorial acknowledgement on dark surface.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: A dialog interrupts. Reserve it for a self-contained task the participant should finish or dismiss before moving on — scheduling a call, reviewing a partner's profile — never for content that belongs on the page. Every dialog is a rounded-2xl parchment popup with a 1px border and a 4px ochre-700 strand across its top edge, laid over a spruce-tinted backdrop that dims the page behind it. A ghost icon close sits in the top-right corner; footer actions align to the right.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Tooltips carry supplementary hints — most often the reason an action is unavailable — on a compact spruce-800 surface with on-dark text. They are deliberately rare in the app: use one only when a control needs a short explanation that would clutter the layout if shown inline, and never for information a participant must not miss (that belongs in an Alert) or as a control's only accessible name.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Context-only clarification, never critical instructions.

components.name: Toast
components.description: A toast tells a participant an action worked (or didn't) and then disappears. Use it for transient confirmations — "Settings saved.", "Match approved and participants notified." — where the outcome doesn't need to persist on screen. Anything the participant must not miss, or must act on, belongs in an inline Alert instead, which stays put until it's resolved.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Transient confirmation that does not block progress.

components.name: Alert
components.description: An alert stays on the page until the situation it describes changes, which is what sets it apart from a Toast: use it for status a participant needs to keep seeing — "You're on the waitlist.", "This connection is under review." Each alert is a rounded-xl banner with a single border-and-tint pair drawn from one meaning, leading with a bolded sentence and an optional description beneath.

api.name: Usage
api.description: An alert stays on the page until the situation it describes changes, which is what sets it apart from a Toast: use it for status a participant needs to keep seeing — "You're on the waitlist.", "This connection is under review." Each alert is a rounded-xl banner with a single border-and-tint pair drawn from one meaning, leading with a bolded sentence and an optional description beneath.

components.name: Notification center
components.description: The bell lives in the spruce app header. It shows an ochre count of unread notifications, and opening it reveals a scrollable parchment panel of the twenty most recent. New notifications arrive live over a realtime subscription — each one both prepends to the panel and raises a Toast with a "View" action. Clicking a row marks it read and routes to the connection or dashboard it concerns.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Bell trigger with recent notifications panel.

components.name: Cohort circle
components.description: The cohort circle answers one question at a glance: *how close is this region to gathering?* Seats sit evenly around a ring, one per eligible participant, and the centre always shows the running count. Nothing about the meaning depends on colour alone — the number and the outlined empty seats carry the same information for anyone who can't distinguish spruce from ochre.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Seat-by-seat readiness indicator.

components.name: Journey stepper
components.description: The stepper turns a form or wizard into a walk with a visible destination. Three states read at a glance: a **completed** step is a solid spruce circle with a check, the **current** step is a solid ochre circle showing its number, and an **upcoming** step is a hollow outline. The rail between steps fills spruce up to the current position, so progress is legible from the connecting line alone.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Sequential orientation through onboarding or learning.

components.name: RTR brand
components.description: The mark is two arcs — ochre and river — that together form a single circle around two dots: two people held by one relationship. The circle is **open at the top and bottom**, so the relationship is never closed to others. A muted variant drains the colour, removes the dots, and dashes one strand; it stands in wherever a relationship hasn’t formed yet, most often inside an empty state. The woven strand echoes the same two colours as an interlacing divider.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Open-circle mark and two-line wordmark.

components.name: Message bubbles
components.description: A connection chat is the first real conversation between two matched people, so the bubbles are calm rather than app-loud: generous radius, quiet borders, and only two colours. **Your** messages align right in a spruce-100 bubble; **their** messages align left in parchment, led by the sender’s avatar. Each bubble’s corner nearest its sender is tightened, giving a subtle tail without a drawn pointer. A day divider separates conversations across dates, and a small meta line under each bubble carries the sender, time, and — for your own messages — whether it has been read.

api.name: Usage
api.description: Alternating conversation bubbles.
